title: Me'irat Einayim on Shulchan Arukh, Choshen Mishpat
text: 1. Today, dayanim judge — based on what is written in the Torah, "Shoftim v'shotrim titen lecha b'chol she'arecha" etc.Today, dayanim judge — based on what is written in the Torah, "Shoftim v'shotrim titen lecha b'chol she'arecha" etc. The Tur wrote, and these are his words: We conclude in the Gemara, the first perek of Makkos, that in Eretz Yisrael we are obligated to appoint judges in every pelech (district) and every city, and in chutz la'aretz we are obligated in every pelech but not in every city. And this is specifically at a time when there is semicha, but nowadays, when there is no semicha, all dayanim are bateil min haTorah, as it is written "v'eileh ha'mishpatim asher tasim lifneihem" — "before Elokim," which is written in the perek, meaning before the semuchim, not hedyotos, and we are hedyotos. Therefore we do not judge min haTorah; rather, we act as shluchaihu d'kamai (the agents of the earlier ones, the semuchim from earlier generations). And we conclude that we only act as their shluchim in matters that are shechiach and involve chisaron kis, etc. See there. And with this, the words of the Mechaber will be clear to you, and see what I will write for you further on in explaining his words. The Tur further wrote (as it appears in the Gemara, first perek of Sanhedrin): R' Yirmiyah said, "asher tasim lifneihem" — it should have said "asher telamdem"; rather, these are the kelei ha'dayanim (the implements of the judges), etc. And Rav Hai wrote: A beis din needs to have prepared, at the seat of the beis din, a staff to strike with, a strap to flog with, and a shofar to place people in nidui with, etc. And it is surprising to me regarding the Mechaber and the Rema z"l that they omitted this. And also, I have not seen the elder rabbanim being careful about this — that they should have before them these implements mentioned above. And perhaps they hold that this was only required for dayanim semuchim, since "tasim lifneihem" is written. But the plain language of Rav Hai mentioned above, and the Tur who brings him, does not seem to indicate this. And it requires further study.

2. "Dinei hoda'os v'halva'os" — the language of the Tur. The explanation: that he claims against him with eidei hoda'ah (witnesses to an admission), meaning that [the defendant] admitted to him in their presence, or that [the plaintiff] lent to him in their presence. End [of the Tur's quote]. And the same applies if he claimed him for a loan without witnesses. And regarding shevu'as heses, see the Prishah.

3. "And there is chisaron kis in them" — also in inheritances and gifts, according to the words of the claimant, there is chisaron kis in them. And the reason in all of them is so that the door should not be locked before borrowers, and so that the door should be locked before one who acts wrongly — [therefore] the Rabbanan said to act as shluchaihu d'kamai. And it appears to me that the same applies to other significant matters, for we have found that they said to accept geirim in the present time even though it is not shechiach, and we have also found that they would compel gittin in Bavel even though there is no chisaron kis in them — as the Ran and Beis Yosef wrote, see there, and in the Darchei Moshe and in his hagahos, se'if 4.

4. "Such as an animal that injured, etc." — The Mechaber adopted here the language of the Rambam at the beginning of perek 5 of Sanhedrin. And he [the Rambam] called a tolda of keren — which is not its way (orchah) and not the manner of its benefit — "chavalah." And therefore he wrote without qualification here and wrote "we do not judge them," and it is not specifically that it injured another [animal], but rather the same applies to anything it damaged in a matter that is not its way, as the Tur wrote. And what is its way or the manner of its benefit is not called chavalah but rather hezeika. And that is what he writes immediately afterwards in chelek gimmel: "And likewise an animal that damaged with shen and regel, etc." until "and the dayanim of chutz la'aretz collect it" — and so it is in the Rambam there. And it deals even with one that injured another, since the Gemara explicitly says that "shor on shor" — we judge in a matter that is its way. And this is straightforward (kashya li — i.e., the matter is clear).

5. "Such as tashlumei kefel" — The Mechaber follows the language of the Rambam, who wrote so in perek 5 of Sanhedrin. And it requires study (tzarich iyun): kefel in any case is not collected in Bavel because it is a kenas, as the Rambam wrote there — that only semuchim collect it — and as the Mechaber also wrote there afterwards. And the Tur did not write kefel, but only boshes. And also in the earlier part, regarding matters that are not metzuyim but have chisaron kis in them, the Rambam and the Mechaber did not write "such as an animal that injured another," which is a tolda of keren as above and is called kenas — rather, [the Tur] wrote "such as a person who injured a person," and so it is in the Gemara in both [places] in Perek HaChovel. And one can say: since the fact that we do not collect boshes and nizkei adam b'adam is also because they gave it the din of kenas — for a matter that is not shechiach or that has no chisaron kis in it, as is written in the Gemara and as I wrote in the Drishah, see there — therefore the Rambam took in his language matters that are kenas themselves, as a clearcut case (l'davar peshitus), and the same applies to anything where you find that Chazal gave it the din of kenas.

6. "Like one who tokei'a [blasts in the ear of] his fellow" — The Rambam and the Mechaber adopted the plain language of the Mishnah in Perek HaChovel (daf tzaddik). And see further in siman 420 se'if 41, where he wrote its explanation: "tak'a chaveiro b'kapo" (he blasted his fellow with his palm) — he pays a sela; "satro al panav" (he slapped him on his face), etc. And this is the explanation of the Rambam, see there. And Rashi and the Ran explained it differently, see there in Perek HaChovel. And see Rashi there (daf 84 amud beis), where it is implied that anything whose damages are not fixed (kitzuvin) is not called kenas — but even so, anything that is not shechiach and has no chisaron kis in it is not collected in our times. And they [Chazal] called it in their language "kenas" on account of the fact that Chazal gave it the din of kenas with respect to this matter — that we do not collect it in our times. And so it is proven in Tosafos of Perek HaManiach and of Perek HaChovel, and as I wrote in the Prishah and Drishah, and also immediately below in the Sma.

7. "More than what he damaged" — such as a thief who pays kefel, [for] slaughtering and selling [pays] four and five, and if he stole and swore [falsely] he pays keren and chomesh, and shor tam [pays] chatzi nezek. And what he wrote, "except for chatzi nezek tzeroros" — the explanation: an animal that walked in reshus harabim and kicked with its legs and through this broke vessels, which is damage that comes via tzeroros (pebbles). And it is its way (orchah), and it is a tolda of regel. And by strict law, the owner should pay nezek shalem, except that it is a halacha l'Moshe miSinai that it only pays chatzi nezek — as the Tur and the Mechaber wrote later in siman 390, see there.
8. "Mumchin" — meaning a person who is experienced (menuseh) and expert (baki) in laws (dinim), as is written in siman 3 se'if 2.

9. "The semuchim" — In the Rambam at the beginning of perek 4 of Sanhedrin it is explained that the term semicha spread from what is written in the Torah (regarding Moshe with Yehoshua): "vayismoch yadav alav vayitzaveihu" (and he placed his hands upon him and commanded him), and likewise he did to the zekeinim, and through this the Shechinah rested upon them. And semicha throughout the generations was not via the laying of the hand, but rather they call him "Rabbi" and say to him: "you are hereby samuch and you have authority to judge even dinei kenasos." And because all of those receiving semicha needed to be musmach specifically from one of the musmachim — man from man back to Yehoshua who was musmach by hand, as the Rambam wrote there (unless through the gathering of all the chachmei Eretz Yisrael together, as he wrote there) — and therefore it is called semicha. And see in the Rivash, end of siman 241, where he wrote the matter of the semicha that the Ashkenazim practice, and the Rama brought it in Yoreh Deah siman 242 se'if 14, see there. And what the Mechaber is precise about and writes "mumchin who are semuchim in Eretz Yisrael" — and likewise he is precise after this in se'if 2, and likewise at the beginning of siman 2 — this is from what the Rambam wrote in perek 4 of Sanhedrin, where he wrote, and these are his words: "Elokim is called only a beis din that received semicha in Eretz Yisrael alone, and they are the chachamim who are fit to judge, whom the beis din of Eretz Yisrael examined and appointed them and ordained them, etc., until: we do not ordain zekeinim in chutz la'aretz even if the one giving semicha is in Eretz Yisrael and the one receiving it is in chutz la'aretz, and kal v'chomer the opposite, etc., until: a beis din who were ordained in Eretz Yisrael and went out to chutz la'aretz — they judge dinei kenasos in chutz la'aretz, etc." — see what he wrote.

10. "Nezek, tza'ar, and pegam, etc." — The Rambam and the Tur did not include them in this principle, since kofer does not apply to ordinary chavalah, only nezek, tza'ar, and boshes. And pegam is not mentioned in the Gemara and poskim regarding chavalah, only in a place where nezek is not mentioned. And here, since the Mechaber already wrote "nezek," we need to explain that what he wrote — "and pegam" — refers to ones (rape) and mefateh (seduction), and it is in the place of nezek shalem, as Rashi wrote at the beginning of Perek HaChovel (Bava Kama daf 84, beginning of amud beis). And kofer applies to a shor that killed a person. And the Mechaber was brief and included them together. And see in the Prishah and Drishah there, where I wrote: the reason we do not collect pegam — even though at the beginning of Perek HaChovel we say regarding it that it is shechiach and also has chisaron kis in it — is because the Gemara did not say that it is shechiach except for the assessment (shuma) [itself] of what difference there is between a besulah and a be'ulah, since everyone is experienced in the matter of marriage, and it is not included in their statement "anything that is appraised like a slave, etc." But the act itself — to be ones or to seduce besulos — that is not shechiach, [and therefore] we do not act as shluchaihu.

11. "But sheves and ripui we collect" — the explanation: from every chavalah we collect, even from cutting off his hand, which is not shechiach. Nevertheless, since sheves and ripui also apply to other blows and wounds that are shechiach, the Rambam holds that we do not distinguish between one blow and another, and we collect from all of them. And the Rosh holds that we do not collect [in non-shechiach cases]. And in the Prishah I wrote the reason for the machlokes between the Rambam and the Rosh, see there.

12. "And I have not seen them practicing, etc." — In the Darchei Moshe se'if 4, [the Rama] wrote this on the basis of the rulings of the Mahari Weil (Mahara"i), whom he brought there, who wrote in siman 208 that we collect ripui and sheves and fine him, etc. And the implication of his language there is that even in the present time we act this way. And on this Morenu Harav Moshe [the Rama] wrote there, and these are his words: "I have not seen them practicing to collect sheves; rather, we obligate him to heal him and to fine the chovel according to what appears to the dayanim," see there. And here in the hagahah, [the Rama] did not mention that we obligate him to heal him, and he included the cost of healing within the cost of placation (piyus). And what he wrote, "and I have not seen them practicing thus" — it appears that this refers to what the Mechaber wrote, "to collect sheves and ripui." On this the Rama wrote "and yeish omrim, etc." — meaning that he too did not see [the practice of] being precise to force [the chovel] to pay sheves and ripui according to the assessment (shuma), but only to force him to placate [the nichbal].

13. "An animal that damaged a person, etc." — (in Bava Kama daf 2) the reason is explained: because a person has mazal. And Rashi explained: a person, who has the faculty of intellect (bar sechel), guards himself.

14. "And yeish omrim, only gezeilos, etc." — See the Nimukei Yosef, who wrote so to reconcile the Gemaros with each other. But the Tosafos there on daf 84, and in the last perek of Gittin on daf 88, and in the first perek of Sanhedrin on daf 3, divided differently and wrote: only gezeilos that come by way of chavalos do we not judge. And this is the view of the Mechaber, who wrote without qualification that we do judge gezeilah. And see in the Darchei Moshe se'if 4.

15. "Eidim who testified false testimony" — it appears straightforward that Morenu Harav Moshe [the Rama] did not write this to explain dina d'garmi, since dina d'garmi is explained there later in siman 386 differently. Rather, the Rama wrote it as a din unto itself. And it is from the Mordechai at the beginning of Perek HaChovel, where they wrote it as a din unto itself.

16. "And they were hozmim and they extracted, etc." — specifically when [money] was extracted through them, then [the zomemim] are obligated, and not from [the principle of] "ka'asher zamam" (as he plotted) when they had not yet extracted [the money], since that is a kenas. And the reason he wrote "they were hozmim" and not "they were huk'cheshu" (contradicted) is because in [a case of] hak'chashah — two said "he borrowed" and money was extracted on the basis of their testimony, and after some time two came and said "he did not borrow" — in such a case, if money had been extracted on the basis of their testimony, we do not obligate them [the first witnesses to repay], because what reason do you have to believe the latter [pair] more than the former? This is unlike if they were hozmim. And as the Tur and the Mechaber wrote later at the beginning of siman 31, siman 35, and siman 46 se'if 37.

17. "And once he gives him the appropriate amount we release him" — as the language of the Mechaber. So is the language of the Rambam at the end of perek 5 of Sanhedrin. And he wrote there further, and these are his words: "we release him whether or not his litigant is appeased (nispayeis)." And it appears that we need to emend [the text] here in the words of the Mechaber accordingly. And what he wrote, "once he gives the appropriate amount" — it appears that he does not mean specifically the full damages, but rather close to that amount. And so the Tur wrote in the name of Rav Sherira and the Rosh, that close to the amount of his damage suffices, see there. And the Rambam adopted the language of the Rif, who wrote that such is the practice of the yeshivos. And in the Drishah I proved that the view of the Rif is also so, see there. And now it makes sense that he needed to write that we release him even if his litigant is not appeased — meaning, even though [the nichbal] wants him to pay the full damages [before being released]. And it also makes sense that he concluded and wrote, and these are his words: "and likewise, if the nizak seized [property], etc., we do not extract from his hand, etc." — for the difficulty is: what does "and likewise" mean here? Isn't this a kal v'chomer? Rather, certainly he comes to teach us that even if he seized the full amount of his damages, we do not extract from his hand. And so the Tur wrote in the name of the Rosh, that we do not extract from his hand except for the surplus beyond his damages. One can also say that included in "what is appropriate for him to take" — as he said — is also kefel and daled v'hei, which we likewise do not extract from his hand, as is written in the next subsection. And the language "and likewise" — the explanation is: even though the dayanim, etc., do not collect kenasos, nevertheless there is a remedy for the nizak, etc., by way of placing the mazik in nidui, etc., and likewise there is a further remedy if he seized.

18. "We do not extract from his hand" — the explanation: even if he seized more than the amount of his damage, if [the mazik] would have been obligated to him for that amount [had they been judging him] — such as kefel, daled v'hei — his tefisah is a [valid] tefisah. And so the Rosh and the Tur wrote at the end of siman 349, and see the Prishah. And so it is proven from the words of Morenu Harav Moshe in siman 348 se'if 4, see there. And in the Ir Shushan, he wrote that even without tefisah — when we place [the mazik] in nidui until he placates the nizak — we do not release him from the nidui until he gives close to kefel and daled v'hei, etc. And this is not [correct]. For in siman 349 it is clarified that wherever he did not seize, there is no one who says he should be in nidui until he gives more than the amount of his damage — as I wrote there with a reasoned explanation. And so it is proven from what the Tur wrote in this siman in se'if 1, and these are his words: "And Chazal reasoned that it is fitting that great damage would result from the fact that we do not judge dinei kenasos, and they made a takanah to place the chovel in nidui until he placates the nichbal closely, etc." — implying that specifically over the kenas of chavalah and the like do we place [him] in nidui — [cases] where there is no additional mamon component — and because otherwise everyone would injure and damage his fellow. But not for kefel and daled v'hei, since even if we do not collect them, one cannot say that everyone will steal and rob, given that it is known that he will have to pay [back] his theft and his robbery. And we also hold like the Rosh, who wrote that whether he seized at the time of the damage or after the damage, whether the damaging item itself or something else, his tefisah is a [valid] tefisah. And therefore the Mechaber and Morenu Harav Moshe wrote here without qualification that tefisah is effective. However, the Mordechai at the end of Perek HaManiach wrote the responsum of Rabbeinu Baruch: that for nezek of keren we act like Rabbeinu Tam, and for other kenasos like the view of those who disagree, see there, and in the Darchei Moshe se'if 6, who brought it. And also the Mechaber wrote without qualification, and did not write that if [the mazik] admitted to the kenas the tefisah does not help him, because we hold like the Ramban, that in the present time he is not exempted by his admission, and even if witnesses did not come — and consistent with his [Ramban's] words the Tur wrote without qualification later in siman 348, see there, and see the Drishah.

19. "And such and such you shall return" — this is not like what the Mahari Weil wrote in siman 28, and as is written in the Darchei Moshe, see there. And the Rosh and the Tur concluded on this and wrote, and these are his words: "And if the tofeis did not bring witnesses such that it is fit to acquit him through them [the witnesses], we say to him to return what he seized." End [of quote]. And Morenu Harav Moshe wrote on this, and these are his words: "That is specifically if he seized with witnesses [present]. But if he seized without witnesses, he is believed with a migo of 'I did not seize.'" End [of quote]. And the meaning is along the lines of what will be explained later at the end of siman 87 se'if 30, see there, regarding a monetary claim. And also regarding a kenas claim, migo is effective, as the Mordechai wrote at the end of Perek HaManiach, and the Tur at the end of siman 399 (and also Morenu Harav Moshe wrote so there in se'if 4), and the responsum, see there, and see the Drishah.

20. "In kenasos that are written" — and the Mordechai wrote in Perek HaSholeach in the name of the Ri: that even though we do not collect kenasos in the present time, nevertheless they can be judged based on [the authority of] the shiv'ah tovei ha'ir (the seven leading men of the city). And see in siman 2.

21. "But kenasos, etc." — In the rulings of the Mahara"i siman 64, it is implied that one can fine someone who refuses to be tziyas din (compliant with the court's judgment) — that he should give a fine to the king. And the Darchei Moshe brought this at the end of siman 3. And see further in siman 388 se'if 5 in the Sma, what I wrote there.

22. "One who shames with words" — this too the Tur wrote in the name of Rav Sherira and the Rosh, and it is from the takanas ha'geonim. But min ha'din, [the mevayesh b'dvarim] is patur from boshes devarim, and even with dayanim semuchim we do not collect boshes from him min ha'din, as is in Perek HaChovel (Bava Kama daf 91 amud aleph). And this is not like what is written in the Ir Shushan, see there.

23. "According to his honor" — in the Yerushalmi (the Tur brought it): one who shames a zaken (elder) gives him a litra d'dahava (litra of gold). End [of quote]. And it is a weight of 35 dinarim of gold, as the Rambam wrote — the Tur brought him later in siman 420 se'if 30, where he wrote: "and we collect from him 35 gold dinarim." And it is proven from what he concludes there after this, that it is a litra of gold, see there. And some explain that it is 36 gold [coins], as is written in Yoreh Deah siman 334 in the name of the Maharam Mintz.
1. "Every court", even a court outside of Israel
2. "Even though they are not semuchin in Eretz Yisrael". See what I wrote in the siman before this, at the end of se'if katan 8. Its explanation is:

3. "that the people are unrestrained, etc.": See in the Prishah there. I wrote that even though not all the people are unrestrained, but rather an individual among them, they can punish that individual and fine him outside the letter of the law according to what their eyes see. But when the people are unrestrained, they can enact and fence in all the people and punish each one who transgresses their enactment, even though they did not see that man as one who was unrestrained in his deeds, but rather in order to fence in the people. See there, and it is easy to understand.

4. They judge both death [and money], etc.: meaning, even one who is not liable to death. And so wrote the Rambam, and the Tur cited it. And see the Prishah and Drishah, what I wrote there in the name of the Nimukei Yosef.

5. And even where there is no complete testimony in the matter, and even without warning, for one does not require witnesses and warning except to judge by Torah law. But one who transgresses the ordinances of the state, they can act according to the need of the hour. So wrote the Ramban in a responsum, siman 279.

6. And even where there is no complete testimony, etc.: The Beis Yosef wrote in the name of the Rashba, of blessed memory, that for capital cases they must be cautioned to act with the agreement of the elders of the city, so that they act after great need and with deliberation. End quote.

7. They strike him by means of a non-Jew: from the fact that he did not conclude by writing "and we say to him, do what the Jew tells you," as the Tur wrote, it implies that he holds that even the final judgment they may carry out by means of a non-Jew, since he is a violent man, and especially when they are coming to fine him, for that is not [strict] law. And see the Prishah, what I wrote about this.

8. And they have the power to declare ownerless, etc.: and he concluded there, in these words: and to fine a violent man, and to place him under niduy, and to place him under cherem, and to curse him, and to strike him, and to pull out his hair, and to bind him in the prison house, and to make him swear by the Name that he did not do and that he will not do these things; and in all this his intent (meaning, the intent of the judge) shall be for the sake of Heaven, and let the dignity of others not be light in his eyes, etc. And he wrote further there: and likewise they flog and disgrace one whose reputation is bad, etc. And in the Beis Yosef and the Darchei Moshe they cited what the Ran wrote on this: and this applies to an ordinary person, but a Torah scholar — "cover him completely like the night." End quote. And it is from the Gemara in Menachos, chapter Shtei HaLechem, in these words: Reish Lakish said, a Torah scholar who has sinned, one does not place him under niduy in public, as it says (in Hosea 2): "and you shall stumble by day, and the prophet also shall stumble with you by night" — cover him like the night. End quote.

9. That the beis din has appointed them over them: the language of the Tur is "that the public has appointed them over them." And according to what the Mechaber wrote, "beis din," it appears that he means that the public appointed the beis din over them. And it is easy to understand.

10. And so they practice, etc.: the language of the Mordechai, beginning of the second chapter of Bava Metzia, in the name of a responsum of Rabbeinu Gershom: anyone who has been appointed over the public, he is like the mightiest of the mighty, and Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation, and whatever he did is done. And so the Rashba wrote, siman 729, that every community in its place is like the Geonim to all Israel, who enacted many enactments for all Israel.

11. Even though there is, etc.: and so wrote the Maharik in shoresh 8 and in shoresh 14, who wrote that even according to the one who holds that the town's leaders can enact whatever they wish, that is specifically regarding what is for the needs of the community; but to expropriate money from one person to another, which is not a communal need, it is obvious that they cannot. And so it implies in the Piskei Maharai, siman 273, and that we do not say hefker beis din hefker except with a great one who has none like him in his generation.
12. Or that he accepted upon himself, etc.: meaning, that then, through speech alone, it is established, even in a matter that was not the prior practice there.

13. And there is loss to this one, etc.: in the Darchei Moshe he wrote that the Mordechai concluded and wrote on this: "and if it is not for the sake of fencing the matter [l'migdar milsa], we do not listen to them." End quote. And it implies from this that for the sake of fencing the matter, all agree that the town's leaders have power. And according to this, one must say that Rema did not write "there are those who disagree" except on what was said, "that so they practice," meaning that they practice this even without a need of the hour, [namely] for fencing the matter; and if so, he was brief in a place where he should have been expansive and explained. And know that I have seen that it is written in the Mordechai "lav migdar milsa," with "lo" [spelled] without a vav and "lo" before "migdar" with a lamed; and according to this it appears that he means: any case like this is not included in the permission of fencing the matter, and we do not listen to them. And it is possible that this is what Rema intended, and for this reason he did not mention it here at all. But it is forced to explain so, and it requires further study.

14. And all the more so if they accepted them, etc.: and the Mordechai wrote in Bava Basra, folio 249, column 3, that the people of the city are not permitted to establish any matter where there is an expert judge or an important person in the city. So wrote Rabbeinu and the Mechaber further on, at the end of siman 231. And there are those who say this is specifically in a matter that is a fine. And all this the Darchei Moshe cited; see there.

15. He gives forty gold pieces: and Maharam Mirzburg wrote: one who is fined a maneh by law absorbs forty; for two hundred, eighty; for each maneh, forty. End quote. And the Darchei Moshe cited it on the words of the Mahari"v mentioned above (who said that forty gold pieces is in place of lashes) in the language of a dispute; and also in the Shulchan Aruch he wrote only the words of the Mahari"v. And see what I wrote in the glosses to the Darchei Moshe, and see further siman 420, se'if katan 41, what I wrote there.

16. But in the hand of the beis din: it is written in the Hagahos Maimoni, chapter 7 of Sanhedrin, [there was] an incident with one who sat on the ground to be flogged and the appointed officer did not come to flog him, and they exempted him, and he brought a proof for the matter; see there what he wrote further from the laws of flogging.

1. A beis din is never fewer than three — this is rabbinic, but by Torah law, in monetary cases, one judge suffices. And so the Rambam writes explicitly in perek 2 of Sanhedrin, that he paskens like Rav Acha; and so it is implied in the Rosh at the end of the first perek of Sanhedrin, and not like what is written in the Ir Shushan — see there.

2. For it is impossible that there should not be among them one who knows sevaros, etc. — the language of the Tur: it is impossible that there should not be among them one who is gamir, who has heard or has read in the seforim and knows the reasonings in the dinim, end quote. And this is not the "gamir and savir" mentioned in the Gemara and poskim, for that one is called a mumcheh and may judge alone — and see the Perishah.

3. That he does not wish to litigate with the plaintiff — in siman 13 it will be explained that only the defendant cannot push him off from litigating with him in his city, but the plaintiff can compel him to go with him to the beis havaad. And to the great beis din the defendant too can push him off — see there.

4. Fewer than three, no, etc. — and so the Rambam writes in perek 2 of Sanhedrin, to the exclusion of the Mordechai in perek 2 of Sanhedrin, and the Hagahos Maimoniyos there, and in the Rambam there. And in the Tur he writes further that if one took authority from the Reish Galusa or from the Nasi who is in Eretz Yisrael, he may judge alone even if he is gamir but not savir — only because we now have neither a Nasi nor a Reish Galusa to take authority from, and as the Tur writes, therefore the Mechaber did not want to go at length into the details of this din, and relied on what he writes at the end of this siman, that one who is not a mumcheh, etc., even though he took, etc. — that we should derive from it that for a mumcheh, taking authority does help. And this is easy to understand.

5. Or one who is an expert to the public — this is the language of the Tur: anyone who is esteemed like Rav Nachman in his generation, expert in Mishnah and Talmud, expert also in judgment, and has reviewed cases for many years and they have tested him many times and found no error in him — such a one was an expert to the public, end quote. And the meaning of "mumcheh" is "tested," as we say regarding going out on Shabbos, that one may go out with an amulet that is mumcheh — and see the Perishah.

6. And nowadays we do not judge, etc. — and so the Tur writes in Yoreh Dei'ah siman 228 regarding the annulment of vows by a single expert, and in siman 334 regarding the giving of a litra of gold to one who shames a talmid chacham.

7. And they are not experts to the public — this implies that if they are experts, even if they are fewer than three, an admission made before them is a valid admission; and so the Tur writes in the name of the Rosh. But the Rambam holds that his admission is not a valid admission even if they are experts and ordained, unless they are three — and then even with laymen it suffices. And this is what the Mechaber concludes when he writes "even if they are ordained," for whoever is ordained is presumably an expert; and so the Rambam writes explicitly, "even if he is an expert." And even though the Rambam wrote this about an individual who is an expert, presumably one must say the same even when there are two experts, as long as they are not three. And it is astonishing regarding the Rama that he mixed the two opinions together and did not write them in the language of a dispute, as the Tur wrote them, that they argue with one another. And one cannot say that he holds the Rambam concedes in the case of an expert to the public, for in the Maimoni it is written there explicitly that even with an expert to the public and ordained the din is so. (And in the Perishah I wrote the reason why the Tur omitted, in the name of the Rambam, the words "expert to the public.") And one can answer, with difficulty, that what the Rama wrote "expert to the public" means that the public appointed them over themselves, for in such a case it does help.

8. He is not established as a denier — that is, as long as he did not say before them "you are my witnesses," for this is effective according to all opinions, for all witnesses, as the Tur and the Mechaber write in siman 32, and in chapter 1 regarding admission, and in siman 79 regarding being established as a denier. And even without "you are my witnesses," whenever he spoke before them in the language of a complete admission, the Rambam who holds this view holds that it is effective; and here it deals with where he did not speak before them in the language of a complete admission — see there.
9. Even though a single expert to the public is permitted, etc. — the Tur wrote this regarding one who took authority; and see the Perishah and Derishah.
10. That he should seat others with him — so is the language of the Rambam, "others," and the language of the Tur is "that he should seat another with him" — and see the Perishah.

11. And it is better that he should decide the din with eleven, etc. — for when they are many they all examine carefully, and the din comes out truer. And what he says "with ten" is not precise, for that would be an evenly balanced beis din; and see the Perishah, where I wrote there why he took the measure of ten and eleven.

12. And it is necessary that all who sit in the beis din be talmidei chachamim and fit — that is to say, all ten mentioned above who sit in the beis din; but it does not refer to a student who sits before his teacher, for as is the implication of the Beis Yosef there, he need not be a talmid chacham, only that he not be an ignoramus.

13. Until he knows with whom he sits — in the responsa of the Mahari Weil siman 147 he wrote to the Maharash, of blessed memory: "And if you will heed my advice, do not sit with the community in any din, for you know that the rulings of the laymen and the rulings of the learned are two opposites; and they said in perek Zeh Borer that this is what the refined ones of Yerushalayim used to do — they would not sit in judgment unless they knew who would sit with them, etc." — see there.

14. One who is not an expert, etc. — meaning that he is neither gamir nor savir; for one who is gamir but not savir is called a stam "mumcheh" in the Rambam's terminology, and taking authority is effective for him, while one who is gamir and savir is called "mumcheh to the public" in the Rambam's terminology. All this I have proven in the Perishah — see there.

15. His ruling is not a [valid] ruling. And the Rambam and the Tur concluded on this, in their language: "And if he erred and engaged in the matter by hand, he is liable to pay, etc." — see the Perishah and Derishah.

16. And he was judged before a beis din — in the Tur it is written "before another beis din," but in the Rambam the word "another" is not written; and indeed it is not needed, for these who judged are not called a beis din, and therefore he wrote that they may go back and be judged before a beis din. And this is easy to understand. And so the Mechaber writes later at the end of siman 25 — see there.
17. To appoint judges, whomever he wishes — however, he must be gamir and savir, as written before this.

This is the language of the Tur, and in the Prishah I wrote that because of a person's craving and being drawn after money he warned with a doubled warning and wrote very very, and for this same reason the Tur also in Yoreh Deah siman 160 in the law of ribbis warned with this expression and wrote one must be very very careful in the prohibition of ribbis, and also at the beginning of siman 336 in Yoreh Deah he wrote regarding medicine, and these are his words, and he should be very very careful just as it is fitting to be careful in capital cases etc., and that is because of the severity of pikuach nefesh, and likewise he warned regarding the prohibition of arayos in Even HaEzer at the beginning of siman 21, and the father of them all is what the Sages of the Mishnah warned with this same expression when they said very very be lowly of spirit, because it is a person's nature to be drawn after arrogance.

So they proved in the Gemara in Kesubos, that from what is written do not take a bribe, for as to perverting judgment he has already been warned about that, as it is written do not pervert judgment, do not commit injustice in judgment, and the reason is explicit in the verse, as it says for the bribe blinds, and the Sages expounded that shochad is a notarikon of she'hu chad, meaning that the giver and the receiver become one body and it is impossible for him to guard himself from inclining after him, and since it is forbidden to accept it from one it is likewise forbidden to accept from both of them equally, and even from the two of them together, even though that reason does not apply there, and as I wrote in the Drishah, see there.

But without a demand he need not return it, since he accepted it only with the willingness of the giver and in order to vindicate the just, and it is not comparable to ribbis, regarding which it is written and your brother shall live with you, upon you to return it to him so that he may live by it, and see further in the Prishah.

In the Prishah I wrote that it means bribery of matters, like the one who removed a feather from the dayan or covered spittle that was before him, and so it is implied in the Gemara, however even actual bribery of words is likewise forbidden, such as to greet him first when it was not his way to greet him first, and everything of that kind, just as they forbade such things in the prohibition of ribbis as the Tur and the Mechaber wrote in Yoreh Deah siman 160, see there.

That is to say, even if he has not yet lent to him, since he has items to lend, then the borrowing that he borrowed from him does not carry upon it the status of a bribe, for he too is able to borrow from him whenever he wishes, and see further in the Prishah, that so it is proven from the language of the Gemara, and so we are compelled to explain the words of the Tur, and as I wrote in the Prishah, see there.
Even if at the time that he sent it to him his claim was already well known, that he would sue him with that claim. Tur.

And the Mahardach wrote, bayis 26, that this that it is only a matter of piety is where he did so to the dayan not in the presence of his fellow litigant, but in his presence it is certainly forbidden, for his claims will certainly be shut up, and this is easily understood, and see the Darchei Moshe who cited him.
We derive it from what is written, and the kohen who is greater than his brothers, make him great from that which belongs to his brothers.

That is to say, to exclude a case where they dedicated it for some specific purpose, in which case it is forbidden to divert it to another purpose, and as is written in Orach Chaim siman 153 and in Yoreh Deah siman 256, and see further in the Prishah.
This refers to what the Mechaber wrote, and they collect it from the beginning of the year or at its end.
Regarding the sons of Shmuel it is written that they did not walk in the ways of their father and they turned aside after profit, and see the Drishah for what I wrote on this.
Also one who takes payment to testify, his testimony is not testimony, and so it is explicitly in the Mishnah, and the Rama wrote it below in siman 34 se'if 18, see there.

That is to say, and then that judgment is a valid judgment, even though he took payment for other cases that he judged before this one and after it, and it is not comparable to one who transgresses a single sin, all of whose judgments and testimonies are void until he does teshuvah, for it is different here, since he did not transgress a negative commandment, but rather it is on account of a fine, and as the Rosh wrote, and see the Darchei Moshe and his glosses for more on this.

This is the correct reading, v'omer with a vav, and specifically when he stipulated with them at the outset is the law so, that he takes from them the entire wage of the work from which he is idled, and because it is stated only that there shall be no destitute among you, but if he did not stipulate and he judged and afterwards comes to take from them evident schar batalah, they need only give him the measure that a person would be willing to take in order to sit idle from that work from which he was idled, like the law of one who returns a lost object, which will be explained below in simanim 264 and 265, and regarding one who receives a business venture from his fellow with respect to ribbis the Tur and the Mechaber wrote in Yoreh Deah siman 177, and in the law of examining the blemishes of a firstborn animal in Yoreh Deah siman 312, and see what I wrote there further on this.
This is the correct reading, but if it is not evident, for example that he has no known work but rather he says etc., and so it is in the Tur.

Up to the word forbidden. See the Drishah where I wrote that from the teshuvah of the Rosh it is implied, though it is not so well proven, that even in such a case his judgments are void, and specifically in such a case where he said perhaps profit will chance upon me through the purchase of merchandise, which is a matter that does not depend on him and is not so readily available, but if he is a craftsman, even though he is not engaged in his craft at the time that the case comes before him, nevertheless, since the matter depends on him, even though it is an unseemly thing to take any payment lechatchilah, nevertheless his judgment is a valid judgment b'di'eved, and see the Drishah for what I wrote further on this.
See what I wrote in siman 3 on se'if 4, on what he wrote there that all those who sit on the beis din must be talmidei chachamim and fit.

The same applies where both of them are poor or both of them are wealthy, and the Maharshal wrote that it takes the case of a point in favor of a poor person as the stronger case, for even though the honor of his teacher and the honor of the wealthy person rest upon him, even so he should not stay silent.
heTitle: מאירת עיניים על שולחן ערוך חושן משפט
